newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen attracts $1.9 billion in new investments.
newsitem.headline: Yemen attracts $1.9 billion in new investments.

text.p: Yemen said on Monday it has attracted about $1.9 billion since March 1992 in new investments that could create more than 43,000 new jobs.
"Foreign and local investors were granted licenses for 866 new projects capitalised at 189.6 billion rials ($1.9 billion)," an official at Yemen's Investment Authority told Reuters.
Some of the projects were joint ventures with Western and Arab firms.
The official said the majority of licenses granted in September were for service sector firms. He did not give a breakdown of the new projects.
Yemen said on Saturday it planned to retire more than 35,000 civil servants under reforms agreed with the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
The reforms include lifting generous subsidies on foodstuffs and raising fuel, electricity, water and telephone rates.
Unemployment in Yemen has been put at 25 percent since reforms was launched in 1995, down from between 30 and 50 percent a year earlier. ($=100 Yemeni rials)
